description: The Claude browser extension is collected as kind=ext and matched by id.
why: This scenario runs only where a real Claude extension install already exists, so it pins ext >=1 and leaves every other kind open: it does not provision the host and must not assert about software it did not install. The id-matching logic is covered without a VM in test/test_matcher.py, against rows captured from a real install.
known_gaps: CANNOT BE TESTED WITH A REAL INSTALL IN AN UNMANAGED VM. Chrome honours ExtensionInstallForcelist only as an MDM-delivered managed policy; an unenrolled Tart guest has none, so the policy is written and ignored. Measured on macOS 26.6.2 / Chrome 152. This scenario SKIPS (exit 3) rather than failing, and asserts only on a host that already carries the extension.

A planted fixture is not a substitute: osquery derives identifier from the manifest key, which unpacked and sideloaded extensions do not carry, so a planted extension reports an EMPTY identifier. See 40-browser.

Two further ids circulate for Anthropic-related extensions. Neither could be installed, so neither is in the catalog. docs/signature-lifecycle.md covers how an unverifiable identifier is recorded rather than guessed at.

Presence is all this proves. What the extension DOES -- which pages it reads, whether it acts autonomously -- is outside what any osquery table reports. The permissions column carries capability, never use.
